questions.q: Why are S3 bucket names required to be globally unique across all of AWS, not just your account?
options: Because a bucket name becomes part of a DNS hostname (bucket-name.s3.amazonaws.com)
Because AWS charges more for duplicate names
Because bucket names are case-sensitive across accounts
They aren't globally unique — only unique within your account
questions.explain: Bucket names form part of a DNS hostname, so AWS enforces global uniqueness the same way domain names are unique.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid S3 bucket name under the naming rules?
questions.explain: Bucket names must be lowercase, 3-63 characters, with only letters, numbers, hyphens and periods — no underscores or uppercase, and not formatted like an IP address.

questions.q: With versioning enabled on a bucket, what happens when you DELETE an object?
options: S3 adds a delete marker on top of the version stack; prior versions remain recoverable
The object and all its prior versions are permanently erased immediately
Versioning has no effect on DELETE behavior
The delete is blocked until you disable versioning
questions.explain: A DELETE on a versioned object adds a delete marker rather than erasing data — every prior version can still be retrieved or restored.

questions.q: What is the maximum size of a single S3 object, and what upload mechanism is recommended above roughly 100 MB?
options: 5 TB maximum object size; multipart upload recommended above ~100 MB
5 GB maximum object size; no special mechanism needed at any size
Unlimited object size; multipart upload is never necessary
1 TB maximum object size; objects must be pre-compressed
questions.explain: S3 objects can be up to 5 TB, but a single PUT request is capped at 5 GB — multipart upload splits larger uploads into parallel parts, and AWS recommends it above roughly 100 MB.

questions.q: What is user-defined metadata on an S3 object?
options: Custom key-value pairs you attach yourself, separate from the metadata S3 manages automatically
A required field that must match the bucket's naming policy
System-generated data like ETag and content type
questions.explain: User-defined metadata (like x-amz-meta-source) is custom key-value data you attach; system metadata (size, type, ETag) is managed by S3 itself.
